problem.title: Three Names for Seven Tenths
problem.statement: Which row gives three equivalent names for the same number?
hints: Seven tenths is also seventy hundredths.

solutionSteps.title: Rename the parts
solutionSteps.body: 7/10 = 70/100. Seven tenths is 0.7 in decimal form and 70% in percent form.

validationMethods: Independent decimal audit: divide 7 by 10 to get 0.7 and multiply each option's decimal by 100; only A produces the stated percent and fraction.
notes: All distractors change place value rather than preserve magnitude.

problem.title: Five Pieces from Different Cuts
problem.statement: Two equal-length bars are cut into equal pieces. Which comparison is correct?
hints: Both fractions select five pieces; compare the size of one piece.

solutionSteps.title: Compare slice size
solutionSteps.body: Eighths are larger than twelfths when the wholes match. Selecting five of each gives 5/8 > 5/12.

validationMethods: Unit-fraction argument: 1/8 > 1/12, so multiplying both by positive 5 gives 5/8 > 5/12.
Independent cross-product and choice audit: 5×12 = 60 > 5×8 = 40; only C states the resulting order.

problem.title: Order Three Forms
problem.statement: Which is the correct order of 0.45, 1/2, and 48% from least to greatest?
hints: Give all three values decimal names.

validationMethods: Decimal normalization: the values are 0.45, 0.50, and 0.48, giving A.
Independent hundredths placement: 45/100 < 48/100 < 50/100; audit of all five orders leaves only A.
notes: The three forms must be unified before comparison.

problem.title: Percent of Which Whole?
problem.statement: A shelf contains 80 books. Exactly 35% of the books are mysteries. How many mystery books are on the shelf?
hints: The whole is the 80 books; find 35 hundredths of it.

solutionSteps.title: Use the whole
solutionSteps.body: 35% of 80 is 0.35 × 80 = 28. Equivalently, 10% is 8 and 5% is 4, so 30% + 5% is 24 + 4 = 28.

validationMethods: Independent benchmark decomposition: 30% of 80 is 24 and 5% is 4, totaling 28; only choice C matches.
notes: The reference whole is explicit and necessary.

problem.title: Complete the Equivalent Triple
problem.statement: A point on a number line is labeled 0.625. Which pair gives a fraction and a percent for that same point?
hints: Write 0.625 as thousandths, simplify, and then count hundredths.

solutionSteps.title: Find the fraction
solutionSteps.body: 0.625 = 625/1000. Dividing numerator and denominator by 125 gives 5/8.

validationMethods: Independent division and option audit: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625; converting each offered percent to a decimal shows only 62.5% also equals 0.625.
notes: The value complements the lesson's 3/8 example without duplicating it.
